questions.prompt: What does `RAISE_APPLICATION_ERROR(-20001, 'Insufficient balance');` do?

options.text: Raises a custom user-defined error (range `-20000` to `-20999`) back to the caller/client with an explicit message

questions.prompt: What does `PRAGMA EXCEPTION_INIT(e_fk_violation, -2291);` accomplish?

options.text: Associates a named PL/SQL `EXCEPTION` variable with a specific Oracle error code so you can catch `WHEN e_fk_violation THEN` cleanly

questions.prompt: What do `SQLCODE` and `SQLERRM` return inside an `EXCEPTION` handler?

options.text: The numeric Oracle error code (e.g., `-1403`) and the formatted error message string (pair with `DBMS_UTILITY.FORMAT_ERROR_BACKTRACE` for line numbers!)

questions.prompt: What is the key difference between an Associative Array (`TABLE OF ... INDEX BY PLS_INTEGER/VARCHAR2`) and a `VARRAY`?

options.text: Associative arrays are sparse, unbounded key-value maps in PL/SQL memory; `VARRAY` has a fixed upper bound and preserves dense ordering (can be stored in table columns)
Associative arrays can be stored in table columns

questions.prompt: What does `BULK COLLECT INTO l_ids` do in a query?

options.text: Fetches one row at a time
Fetches many rows into a PL/SQL collection in a single SQL-to-PL/SQL context switch (use `LIMIT 500` in a cursor loop for large tables!)

questions.prompt: What does `FORALL i IN 1 .. l_ids.COUNT` do compared to a regular `FOR i IN 1 .. l_ids.COUNT LOOP`?

options.text: Sends the entire array of bind values to the SQL engine in a single context switch, dramatically speeding up bulk `INSERT`/`UPDATE`/`DELETE`

questions.prompt: Why does `l_arr(i)` inside `FORALL` raise an error if `l_arr` is sparse (e.g., elements deleted with `.DELETE(2)`)?

options.text: `1 .. l_arr.COUNT` hits the missing index unless you use `INDICES OF l_arr` or `VALUES OF`

questions.prompt: What does `:NEW.updated_at := SYSTIMESTAMP;` inside a `BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE ... FOR EACH ROW` trigger do?

options.text: Modifies the incoming row's `updated_at` column before it is written to the table

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about the mutating table error (`ORA-04091`) in triggers. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Solved cleanly by using a `COMPOUND TRIGGER` (collecting keys in `AFTER EACH ROW` and querying/updating in `AFTER STATEMENT`)

Occurs when a row-level (`FOR EACH ROW`) trigger tries to `SELECT` or modify the same table currently being modified by the triggering DML

questions.prompt: Why should `WHEN OTHERS THEN NULL;` be avoided in PL/SQL?

options.text: It silently swallows ALL errors (including constraint failures and bugs), corrupting data without any trace

questions.prompt: What does `RAISE;` (with no exception name) inside an `EXCEPTION` block do?

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about `FORALL ... SAVE EXCEPTIONS`. (Select all that apply.)

questions.prompt: What does `DBMS_OUTPUT.ENABLE(NULL);` (in Oracle 10gR2+) do?

options.text: Sets an unlimited `DBMS_OUTPUT` buffer size instead of hitting `ORU-10027: buffer overflow`

questions.prompt: What does `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE NOWAIT` (or `WAIT 5`) do in PL/SQL?

options.text: Acquires row-level write locks immediately (failing fast with `ORA-00054` if locked, or waiting up to 5s) before updating

questions.prompt: What does `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` enable in a multi-worker job queue table?

options.text: Each worker locks and claims the next unlocked pending row without blocking on rows other workers are processing

questions.prompt: What happens if a cursor opened with `OPEN c_emp;` is NOT closed when an exception is raised before `CLOSE c_emp;`?

options.text: It can leak open cursors until `ORA-01000: maximum open cursors exceeded`—always close in `EXCEPTION` or use a cursor `FOR` loop!
